title: RUPlace: Optimizing Routability via Unified Placement and Routing Formulation
problem: Placement optimization in advanced VLSI designs struggles with routing congestion management; existing methods lack theoretical foundations and decouple placement from routing, missing optimization synergies.
motivation: Growing design complexity and integration density make routing congestion a critical bottleneck that placement algorithms must address directly rather than as a post-hoc constraint.
method: ADMM-based placer that alternately optimizes global routing and incremental placement using Wasserstein distance and bilevel optimization. A convex programming model determines optimal cell inflation ratios for global placement while directly minimizing routed congestion.
key_novelty: First ADMM-based unified formulation of placement and routing that theoretically grounds congestion optimization through bilevel optimization and Wasserstein distance metrics.
contributions: ADMM-based unified optimization framework for joint placement and routing
Bilevel optimization formulation with Wasserstein distance for congestion metrics
Convex model for optimal cell inflation-based global placement
Superior congestion reduction vs. OpenROAD, Xplace 2.0, DREAMPlace 4.1

metrics.other: Superior congestion reduction, competitive wirelength and runtime

primary_theme: Unified ADMM-based placement-routing co-optimization for congestion management
